Components / Surfaces

Profile head

.dr-profile · __photo · __badges · .dr-avatar-edit · __badge · .dr-avatar-lg · components/avatar.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Olena B. Verified with Diia
  1. 1.dr-profileA centred column with no card: no ground, no padding, no radius. Standing on the page improves every pair: the name rises from 14.37:1 to 15.99:1.
  2. 2.dr-avatar-editThe link. It wraps the picture and the badge, so the target is the whole 120 × 120 photo, not the disc, and its name is Change profile photo.
  3. 3.dr-avatar-lgThe photo, 120 × 120 at the pill radius, object-fit: cover, on a --media ground for the moment before it decodes.
  4. 4.dr-avatar-edit__badgeThe pencil disc on the circle's edge: --color-action under --on-action at 9.46:1, cut out of the photo by a 2px ring. The ring is a border, not a shadow, so the flat rule holds. It is aria-hidden.
  5. 5.dr-displayThe name, 22/700 at 15.99:1.
  6. 6.dr-chip--claimWhat the platform has confirmed, on --bg-accent-tint at 14.75:1, with a shield and a trailing tick.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Profile head; Profile photo (large); Avatar edit.

States

Light

Dark

Try it: hover, press, Tab. Follows the theme switch above.

The photo link alone, from account. The name and the credential chips take no state.

When to use

The profile head is the top of account and operator-account: the face, the name, and what the platform has confirmed. It is a component of its own and not a modifier of the operator card. That card is a row in somebody else's list, while this column is the subject of the frame. The two heads are the same element with the same classes. Only the credentials differ. The credential sits on the head, before any tap. That is RJ-C1, the highest single drop-off in the CJM.

The photo is the control, and the green disc on it says this can be changed. The disc is not the screen's only green: the floating Edit profile is a solid green primary on both account and operator-account. On the head the disc measures 44 with a 22px pencil, larger than the component's base 20 × 20. The <img> takes alt="" here, because the name is written beside it. On account-photo, where the picture is the content, it carries real alt text (WCAG 1.1.1). The served thumb is 128 × 128 against the 120px box, so a 2× screen upscales it 1.875×. The imagery rule asks for ~240 × 240. This is recorded and left to the designer.

The name is the person's given name and initial: Olena B., Ivan K. Credentials state a fact the platform checked: Verified with Diia, Insured, CAA licence. The name also carries .dr-profile__name, as on the screens. It has no rule of its own; the type comes from .dr-display.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Profile head · § Avatar edit · § Profile photo, large · inventory.md § 1 Profile head, Profile photo (large), Avatar edit · components/avatar.css · ui/kit.html § Profile head

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Ivan K. InsuredCAA licence

The head at the top of the person's own account: one face, one name, and the credentials the platform confirmed, all centred on the page with no card.

Don’t

When the person is someone else, such as the operator a client is waiting for on tracking or order-confirmed, use the operator card. It is a row in a list, carries its own credentials, and has no edit affordance. The head is for one person who is the subject of the screen. Do not wrap it in a card, and do not put the pencil disc on a photo the viewer cannot change.
